passage: They call me "Mr Sincere" at work, and not kindly. I am Ramesh, and last quarter my team wanted to skip the final testing step to hit a release date. I said I would not sign off without it. "Too sincere," someone said. "Not practical," said another. It stung more than I let on, because I do like these people. So I made a joke of it: "Fine, put 'Mr Sincere' on my name plate." They laughed, and the room loosened. Then I stayed late and built a small script that ran the tests in a fraction of the time. Yamini, who had kept quiet, admitted afterwards, "I wasn't comfortable either." We are two now, and I try not to preach. Being practical and honest is possible, just slower to build.
